- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is flat or negative (≤0.00), model underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33 or 0.25 values, model tends to overreact; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast for next 7 days.
